Announcing Fernleaf 2.4 and a year of the garden toolkit

Posted by Mira Okafor on 12 March 2026

A year ago we shipped the first public release of Fernleaf, a small toolkit for planning vegetable beds. Today we are releasing version 2.4 with crop rotation support and a faster planner.

Thank you to everyone who filed bugs, wrote guides and shared their beds with the community. This release is for you, and we hope it makes next season a little easier.

What is in 2.4

The planner now remembers what grew in each bed during the last three seasons. If you try to plant tomatoes where tomatoes grew last year, it will warn you and suggest a better bed.

Planning a 200-bed allotment used to take several seconds. It now finishes in under half a second on a typical laptop, thanks to a rewrite of the scoring loop.

Installing

Update with the package manager of your choice, or download the archive from the download page. The command below works on every platform we support.

$ fernleaf update --channel stable

Stabilized functions

The following functions are now stable and no longer need the experimental flag:

  • Bed::rotate
  • Bed::history
  • Bed::clear_season
  • Planner::score_all
  • Planner::warn_conflicts
  • Planner::suggest_bed
  • Season::next
  • Season::previous
  • Season::span
  • Crop::family
  • Crop::companions
  • Crop::avoids
  • Crop::days_to_harvest
  • Plot::area
  • Plot::split_at
  • Plot::merge_with
  • Plot::into_beds
  • Garden::beds_mut
  • Garden::export_csv
  • Garden::import_csv

A note on soil

Good soil is not something you buy. It is something you feed, season after season, and then leave alone.

That sentence from an early user guide has stayed with the team, and it shaped how we think about the history feature: the garden remembers so you do not have to.

let bed = garden.bed("north-3");
if bed.history().contains(Crop::Tomato) {
    println!("rotate this one");
}

Contributors

Version 2.4 was made possible by forty-one contributors. You can find every name in the thanks page, and the full list of changes is in the changelog.

See you in the beds.
